text:
carmen_support: Customer KitePay reporting SSO failures after an IdP cert rotation. They see 403s for assertion consumer service (ACS) hits and the logs show 'Invalid recipient' with the recipient set to an internal edge host. Repro is intermittent and only from requests that go through their CDN. Can someone triage?

julia_sre: ack, can you paste the exact log line (no PII) and the IdP metadata fetch result? did they rotate signing cert + publish new metadata? :eyes:

carmen_support: log excerpt: `ERROR SAML: Invalid recipient: https://edge-cdn.internal/acs for assertion to https://auth.kitepay.com/saml/acs`
Also we fetched IdP metadata from https://idp.kitepay.com/metadata.xml and it contains ACS https://auth.kitepay.com/saml/acs (single entry). The support engineer says the CDN rewrites Host to `edge-cdn.internal` for caching.

sam_devex: short note — SAML recipient checks are strict (exact string match). If the Host header is rewritten by the CDN/proxy then our platform will see a different recipient. Could be proxy not preserving `Host` or we're reading `X-Forwarded-Host` incorrectly. Can you provide a curl from the origin path?

carmen_support: repro steps from customer: 1) user clicks SSO 2) request goes to CDN 3) CDN hits our platform origin -> we return ACS redirect -> CDN rewrites host and returns assertion to IdP with recipient showing `edge-cdn.internal`
example curl from origin (customer sanitized):
```
curl -i -H "Host: auth.kitepay.com" https://auth.kitepay.com/saml/acs 
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: text/plain

Invalid recipient: https://edge-cdn.internal/acs
```

kai_oncall: seen this before with CloudFront when `Origin Protocol Policy` or `Origin Preserve Host Header` isn't set. CloudFront caches a response and then rewrites the Host on the request back to the IdP, so the Assertion Recipient becomes the CDN host. Quick check: do they have "Preserve Host Header" enabled and are they forwarding the Host header? :hammer:

idp_bot: automated note — IdP cert rotated for idp.kitepay.com at 2026-03-14T02:00Z (rotation-window: 24h). No metadata endpoints failed during rotation window.

julia_sre: actionable items: a) get HTTP access logs showing Host header seen by our service b) check if we use `Host` or `X-Forwarded-Host` when building recipient URL c) ask infra to verify we do not canonicalize to the edge hostname. If CDN is the culprit, recommend customer enable host preservation or use `Origin Host Header` mapping.

sam_devex: short-term mitigations we can suggest to customer: 1) configure CDN to forward original Host (preferred) 2) include the edge host as an allowed ACS entry in their IdP metadata (if they control IdP) 3) add a rewrite in their origin to set `Host: auth.kitepay.com` before processing (nginx example below). Long-term we should consider adding a tolerant recipient check with an explicit header (but that needs security review).
nginx snippet they can use at origin (customer provided):
```
proxy_set_header Host $host;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
```

carmen_support: customer applied "preserve host" on CDN and reports immediate reduction in failures. They couldn't update IdP metadata quickly, so CDN change was the accepted workaround. They're going to monitor.

kai_oncall: will open infra ticket to confirm our front-ends never rewrite Host when proxying assertions; assign to eng-infra and eng-security for review. Ticket: INFRA-12467.

julia_sre: add a follow-up to evaluate if we should log the incoming Host vs expected ACS in failed SAML attempts (only for debug) — helps customers triage without sharing logs.

carmen_support: thanks all — marking as customer-notified, workaround in place. Will re-open if failures reappear. :white_check_mark:
